requirements.evidence: Contract routes and names in routes/web.php:896-920 (guest group for login/register, POST logout with auth, /home with auth+verified, throttle:6,1 on password.email, signed+throttle on verification.verify). Login: strict e-mail via User::EMAIL_RULES 'email:rfc,strict,filter' (app/Models/User.php:433), auth.failed on email (Login.php:294), lowercase e-mail+IP throttle with 5 tries and auth.throttle (Login.php:277-286, 310), session()->regenerate + redirectIntended(route('home')) (Login.php:298-300). Register: key Str::transliterate('register|'.request()->ip()) with 5 attempts and error on email (Register.php:365-374), Password::defaults() configured once in AppServiceProvider.php:456, 'confirmed' on password, Registered event, login, regenerate, redirectRoute('home') (Register.php:389-396). Logout invalidates + regenerateToken (LogoutController.php:155-160). Forgot always flashes RESET_LINK_SENT (ForgotPasswordController.php:129-131). Reset: single name="email" input (reset-password.blade.php:691), remember_token rotated + PasswordReset fired (ResetPasswordController.php:207-212). Verification via EmailVerificationRequest (403 on tampered id), resend no-op for verified users (EmailVerificationController.php:88-90). .env.example and phpunit.xml locale pins present; lang/{en,pt_BR}/ui.php added. Gap: task says the route()-only rule applies to existing views too, but welcome.blade.php / bulma-test.blade.php are not touched in the diff, so that part is not shown to be done.

conventions.evidence: Follows most: Blade components extracted (components/card.blade.php, components/field.blade.php) with @props and {{ }} escaping; Bulma markup; plain wire:model (login.blade.php:827-832); named-route redirects; docs/business-rules.md, README.md and CHANGELOG.md under [Unreleased] updated; $fillable already set on User. Deviations: Livewire components validate via a protected rules() method (Login.php:259, Register.php:349) instead of the project's #[Validate] attribute pattern; ResetPasswordController::store validates three fields inline (ResetPasswordController.php:198-202) where the convention calls for a Form Request beyond two fields; the user write in Register (User::create, Register.php:389) is not in an app/Actions class.

security.evidence: Strong overall: login throttled per lowercased e-mail+IP with Lockout event; register counts every submission (Register.php:377) so unique can't be used to enumerate; forgot-password response identical for unknown/throttled e-mails (ForgotPasswordController.php:129-131); reset maps INVALID_USER to INVALID_TOKEN (ResetPasswordController.php:221); remember_token rotated; EmailVerificationRequest prevents verifying another id; passwords reset on failure and never echoed; all output escaped with {{ }}; mass assignment via #[Fillable(['name','email','password'])]. Minor: the layout falls back to an unpinned-integrity third-party stylesheet 'https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bulma@0.9.4/css/bulma.min.css' with no SRI (layouts/app.blade.php:774).

tests.evidence: Broad Pest coverage: LoginTest (happy path, intended redirect, remember cookie, auth.failed, strict e-mail dataset, throttling with lowercase key, Lockout), RegisterTest (unverified hashed user, Registered, confirmed rule, weak password dataset, uniqueness incl. case variants, IP limiter), PasswordResetTest (non-enumeration, broker throttle, 429 on 7th, single email input, remember_token rotation, PasswordReset event), EmailVerificationTest (tampered id 403 verifies nobody, wrong hash, unsigned, throttling, resend), LocalizationTest (pt_BR/en rendering, key parity), ViewConventionsTest. Missing: no test that an already-authenticated user calling the Livewire submit() action directly (bypassing the guest page middleware) is denied/handled, which the Livewire policy asks for ('unauthorized call to each action'); tamper tests for Livewire only exist indirectly.

simplicity.evidence: Lean controllers using framework primitives (Password broker, EmailVerificationRequest, redirectUsersTo in bootstrap/app.php:469); shared User::EMAIL_RULES avoids duplication; small reusable x-field/x-card. Some unnecessary code: Vite-or-CDN conditional in the layout (layouts/app.blade.php:771-775) is speculative; try/catch only to clear passwords in Register.php:381-387.

readability.evidence: Small focused methods with short docblocks explaining security intent (e.g. ForgotPasswordController.php:120-124, Register.php:358-362); clear names (throttleKey, MAX_ATTEMPTS); consistent typed signatures; no dead code or debug output.

scope.evidence: Nearly everything serves the task (auth flow, lang files, locale pins, docs). Small extras not asked for: CDN Bulma fallback in the layout (layouts/app.blade.php:774) and pt_BR validation attribute names (lang/pt_BR/validation.php:634-639), the latter being a reasonable pt-BR polish. Out-of-scope items (mail theme, Docker/nginx, SCSS/JS) were not touched.

issues.explanation: The task explicitly extends the route()-only link rule to the existing views, but the diff does not touch them, so if they contain hardcoded href="/..." or url('/...') links the requirement is unmet and the new ViewConventionsTest would fail.
Validation is declared with a rules() method instead of the project's #[Validate] attribute pattern for Livewire components.
Three fields are validated inline, whereas the conventions require a Form Request once controller rules grow beyond one or two fields.
Fallback loads Bulma from a third-party CDN without Subresource Integrity, an unnecessary external dependency not requested by the task.
No test covers an authenticated user invoking the Livewire submit() action directly, the unauthorized-call case the Livewire security policy requires for each action.
User creation is done directly in the component rather than through an app/Actions class, which the conventions prefer for writes.
The remember-me test asserts viaRemember() is false, which is irrelevant to the behaviour under test and may confuse readers.

review.summary: The change implements the full session-auth flow (Livewire login/register, logout, home, forgot/reset password, e-mail verification) with pt-BR-first translations, locale pins, docs updates and a thorough Pest suite, and it handles the security details well (throttling, non-enumeration, remember_token rotation, tamper-proof verification). It is approvable with small fixes: the existing views required by the link rule are not shown to be checked or updated, Livewire validation uses rules() instead of #[Validate], the reset controller skips a Form Request, and the layout adds an unnecessary CDN fallback.
